blocks.heading: Groups involved in business
blocks.text: Stakeholders are groups or individuals with an interest in a business’s activities or outcomes. They include consumers, workers, managers, owners, finance providers and the wider community. A person can belong to more than one group: an employee may also buy the product or own part of the enterprise. Their interests should be identified from the business relationship, not from an unrelated category.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: Omuti Foods employs workers, sells to households and has borrowed money for equipment. Workers have an employment interest, households have a customer interest and the lender has a repayment interest. A customer is a stakeholder even without working inside the bakery. A production sector such as manufacturing is an activity classification, not a stakeholder group. Informal friendships among employees are workplace groups, which is another classification again.

blocks.heading: Keeping the ideas apart
blocks.text:
Explain why workers and customers of a bread maker are stakeholder groups, while manufacturing is not a stakeholder group.

Workers have an employment interest and customers have a purchasing interest. Manufacturing describes what the business does, not a group with an interest in its outcomes. Informal friendship groups inside the bakery are another classification and do not replace identifying the relevant stakeholders.
